proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the absence of ontological orientation'?

entities.label: AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation
entities.rationale: The absence of ontological orientation is most plausibly typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (e.g., a legal institution or normative system) and characterizes a measurable or assessable property of that bearer — namely, the lack of directedness toward any ordering principle. It is not a process (it does not unfold as a happening), not a disposition (it is not an internally grounded capacity to behave in a certain way), not a role (it is not externally grounded social function), and not a generically dependent continuant (it is not an information artifact that can be copied). Modeling it as a Quality captures that it is a real but dependent property of some bearer at a time. A subclass relation to BFO_0000019 is proposed. Note: 'absence' in BFO is typically handled by negation or privation modeled as a quality of the bearer rather than as a separate entity; this mirrors how BFO handles e.g. 'absence of pigment' as an albinism quality.

relations.rationale: AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation is a kind of Quality: a specifically dependent continuant inhering in a bearer and characterizing a privative property of that bearer.

open_questions: What is the intended bearer of this absence? E.g., does it inhere in a legal institution (working:LegalInstitution), a normative system, a legal actor, or some other continuant? Specifying the bearer class would allow an owl:Restriction on RO_0000052 (inheres in) to be added.

Is 'ontological orientation' itself to be added as a positive Quality first, with AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation as its privation? If so, should we mint a companion class OntologicalOrientation subClassOf BFO_0000019?

Is this absence intended to relate to any of the existing individuals (e.g., InjusticeAsOntologicalFailureOfAlignment, UnjustLawMisalignmentThesis) as an explanatory component? If so, a relation between those individuals and this class can be proposed.

Should this be treated as an individual (a specific, named absence present in a particular system) rather than a class (a kind of quality)? The answer depends on whether you intend to refer to a single token or to instances in general.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'absence of ontological orientation' names a privative property — the lack of directedness toward an ordering principle — attributable to some bearer (a legal institution, normative system, or actor). In BFO, privations and absences are standardly modeled as Qualities (BFO_0000019) inhering in a bearer, analogous to how 'blindness' is a quality of an eye or organism. It is not a Process (no temporal unfolding as a happening), not a Disposition (no internally grounded causal basis for behavior), not a Role (no externally conferred social function), and not a Generically Dependent Continuant (it carries no information content that can be copied). Accordingly, AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation is proposed as a new class, subClassOf BFO_0000019 (Quality). No individual is minted because the utterance is framed as a general classificatory question ('how would you classify') rather than asserting a specific token. Key open questions concern the intended bearer class and whether a positive companion quality (OntologicalOrientation) should be minted first to ground the privation.
